plan.title: 3 Days in Lisbon: What to See and Eat
plan.description: A three-day Lisbon itinerary covering Alfama, Sintra, Belém and the best local food. Learn where to walk, what to taste and how to order like a local.

beats.narration: Imagine a city where fado drifts down narrow streets at night. Picture an Alfama lane, a yellow tram rattling past, and red rooftops stretching to the river. That is Lisbon, and three days is enough to taste it.
Here is the plan. Day one, get oriented in the old center and Alfama. Day two, dive into food and Belém. Day three, take a day trip to Sintra.
One tip from the guides: choose tours that connect you with locals. A walk with a local guide gives you a view of the city you will not get from a map.

props.text: Choose tours that connect you with locals.

beats.narration: Start downtown. Walk through Baixa under the grand arch on Rua Augusta. Then climb up to Chiado, with its lively streets, shops and cafés, a perfect place to find your feet.
Stop at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara. It looks northeast over the city, and it has a little guide to the hills and landmarks you can see.

props.image_query: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara Lisbon

beats.narration: After lunch, walk five or ten minutes to Castelo de São Jorge. It towers over the city on a hill, with lovely views over the river and, yes, peacocks.
Then wander Alfama, right nearby. Expect narrow streets and colorful buildings. In the evening, fado music drifts through, and Mesa de Frades is a place where fado singers go for inspiration.
Day two is Belém. Start at Belém Tower, a sixteenth-century fortress and UNESCO site right on the water. Then visit the nearby Jerónimos Monastery.
Now the sweet reward. Pastéis de Belém makes and sells about 20,000 custard tarts a day. Manteigaria is another favorite, and you can try it at Time Out Market.

props.label: pastries sold daily at Pastéis de Belém

beats.narration: To eat like a local, find a tasca, a family-run, hole-in-the-wall tavern. Order the bifana, a pork sandwich. Try a prego, a beef sandwich. Then go for sardines and octopus.
Look for the bifana, packed with garlic. Then grilled sardines, and the cozy tasca interior where locals gather. Finish with grilled octopus. Bacalhau, salted cod, is the classic dish.
For a splurge, Belcanto in Chiado, from José Avillez, serves blue lobster and giant red prawns. Reservations are a must, and so is a significant bank account.

props.definition: José Avillez’s Chiado restaurant serving Portugal’s best products with imagination and precision.
props.example: Blue lobster and giant red prawns

beats.narration: Day three, escape to Sintra. It is an easy day trip from Lisbon, and your evening can end back in Chiado over dinner.
So walk the hills, eat in a tasca, and save room for a warm custard tart. Three days will not be enough, and that is exactly why you will come back.
